svg.text: Arduino Uno R3 | AS5600 I2C feedback | DM542 common-anode control | two jog buttons
Power OFF before wiring. Motor DC supply must NEVER connect to Uno 5V. Verify driver voltage limits and ENA polarity.
Hold to jog | release to stop jogging
Identify coil pairs with an ohmmeter
Source: actuator-angle-control/actuator-angle-control.ino. Pin positions are schematic, not physical header order.
Repeated Uno 5V and GND labels are shared rails: use distribution terminals. D0/D1 stay free; commands use USB serial (Newline).
Both buttons: normally open contacts to GND, INPUT_PULLUP, pressed = LOW. On 4-leg switches use opposite switched contacts.
DM542: PUL+, DIR+, ENA+ share Uno 5V; D3, D2, D4 sink the negative inputs. No separate driver '+5V logic' terminal.
Sketch assumes D4 HIGH = enabled, LOW = disabled. Verify ENA behavior and input current on your exact DM542 before running.
Set current and microstep DIP switches per driver/motor manuals. Sketch assumes 400 input pulses per motor revolution.
Use a 5V-compatible AS5600 breakout with suitable I2C pull-ups; OUT/PGO are unused. Strap sensor DIR per module documentation.
Motor power return is separate from the optoisolated signal circuit. E/X are serial hold commands, not additional physical buttons.
